To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we isolated a gene from Sinorhazobium melilotii M5N1 CS that encodes a cellulase, and that this enzyme is active against carboxymethylcellulose.

we cloned, sequenced, and overexpressed the gene encoding EndS, a Sinorhiziobium melilot i carboxymethyl cellulase, that we showed it to belong to family 5 glycoside hyrolases, and that it was active on carboxymethylcellulose, the best substrate tested.
we have isolated, sequenced, and overexpressed the gene encoding the Sinorhizobia meliloti carboxymethyl cellulase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cloning, sequencing and expression of the gene encoding the Sinorhizobia meliloti M 5N 1CS cellulase EndS.
the cloning of the gene encoding a carboxymethyl cellulase from S. meliloti M5 N 1 CS, and the overexpression of the corresponding gene product in E. coli.
the isolation of a gene encoding a β-1,4-glucanase (EndS) from Sinorhazobium melilot i M5N1 CS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this EndS enzyme is a carboxymethylcellulase.
EndS is a CM-cellulase.
this EndS protein is a cellulase, but it is a CM cellulase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
EndS was cloned and expressed and the gene product has a cellulase activity.
the EndS protein is an endo-β-1,4-glucanase that belongs to family 9 of the glycosyl hydrolases.
the EndS protein has a broad specificity and is able to hydrolyze a wide range of β-linked oligo- and polysaccharides.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the EndS enzyme is a novel member of the GH5 family of glycoside hyrdrolases.
the EndS enzyme can be used to produce a range of products, including biofuels, bioplastics, and other materials, from plant biomass.
the EndS protein is the first reported cellulase from a symbiotic nitrogen-fixing bacterium.
